entities.summary: N. D. Cocea was a Romanian journalist, novelist, critic and left-wing political activist, known as a major but controversial figure in the field of political satire. The founder of many newspapers and magazines, including Viața Socială, Rampa, Facla and Chemarea, collaborating with writer friends such as Tudor Arghezi, Gala Galaction and Ion Vinea, he fostered and directed the development of early modernist literature in Romania. Cocea later made his name as a republican and anticlerical agitator, was arrested as an instigator during the 1907 peasant revolt, and played a leading role in regrouping the scattered socialist clubs.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a founder of several influential newspapers and magazines, Cocea played a crucial role in fostering modernist literature in Romania, collaborating with notable writers like Tudor Arghezi. His left-wing activism and republicanism also contributed to the development of socialist clubs, shaping regional politics.
